correctness.rationale: Verified the precise norm N(f)=||f||_infty+sum(w_e|f_i-f_j|), finite simple graph, positive real weights, and path n>=2. The level-set identity f=(1/2)int_{-r}^r s(t)dt and integrated cut weight give an exact convex combination of s/(1+2C_w(s)). The edge-sign linear functional L_s dominates by N(f) with equality only on the positive ray of s, exposing all 2^n vertices even when disconnected. For paths, N is the maximum over j,sigma,epsilon of signed coordinate and edge-difference forms. A unique absolute maximizer with signs forces the two adjacent epsilon constraints. Conversely tiny steps realize an open cone for each such form, hence a true facet. Distinctness of normals and endpoints/interior counting give (n+2)2^(n-2). Retrieved and read verification/verify.py: exact fractions, independent active-vertex rank tests (n<=5 facets, up to n6 vertices) support but do not prove the general result.

value.rationale: The weighted graph total-variation plus sup norm is a natural regularization norm; its exact dual extreme sign signals and complete combinatorial facet count constrain convex optimization geometry. The formula is uniform over arbitrary strictly positive edge weights and all path lengths, more than a numerical instance or reparameterization of a textbook cube. Min-cut threshold characterization is a useful subsidiary computational description.

limitations: Finite simple graphs with strictly positive edge weights; full norm ball in real vertex coordinates, not quotient by constants.
The min-cut statement is a threshold reduction, not a bit-complexity guarantee for arbitrary oracle real weights.
